Definition: from G5259 and G5342; to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship:--bear, endure.
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses hypophérō where we would say to bear up under, to endure. In 1 Corinthians 10:13, the text says "that ye may be able to bear [it]." In 2 Timothy 3:11, the text says "what persecutions I endured."
TheologicalSignificance: What hypophérō teaches me is that endurance is staying under the weight and not giving up, because God is carrying us through it. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
